source_metadata.title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding
source_metadata.file: FutureBridge Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding - 2608.06819v1.pdf

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether token-level SLM-LLM collaboration should select intervention tokens according to how well the receiving SLM can use them for subsequent reasoning rather than according to the LLM's local next-token preference.

The authors identify two gaps in local-preference token selection: a candidate coverage gap when useful LLM candidates are absent from the SLM shortlist and a teaching suitability gap when LLM-preferred tokens are difficult for the SLM to continue from.
FutureBridge formulates collaboration as token reranking over the union of the SLM and LLM top-k next-token candidate sets at states admitted by a fixed request policy.
The ideal token objective is the candidate that maximizes final-answer correctness after the candidate is appended and the fixed deterministic SLM completes the trajectory.
FutureBridge does not optimize the request policy or the per-trajectory intervention budget; these are external and shared across candidate selectors.
Training states are collected by running the frozen SLM under the fixed request policy without inserting candidate interventions or LLM suffixes, so selectors are trained from the same logged states.
For each admitted state, FutureBridge forms a deduplicated union of SLM top-K and LLM top-K candidates, separating candidate availability from candidate selection.

A greedy LLM trajectory from the same state is retained only when its complete final answer is verifier-correct and contains at least 128 post-action tokens; prefixes of this trajectory provide shared futures with horizons 16, 32, 64, or 128 tokens.
Candidate supervision is constructed by replacing only the LLM action token with each candidate while holding the problem, SLM prefix, shared future, and scoring model fixed.

For each candidate, the frozen SLM teacher-forces the shared future and defines future compatibility B_H as the average conditional log-likelihood of the same length-H future after that candidate is inserted.
The B_H compatibility score is a teacher-forced surrogate for complete free-running SLM rollout value and is not a causal final-answer outcome.

FutureBridge standardizes compatibility scores within each candidate group and applies a temperature-scaled softmax to create dense candidate-level targets; pure or hybrid LLM-local-preference targets are retained only as ablations.

A LoRA candidate scorer initialized from the receiving SLM predicts an independent scalar score from only the current state and candidate token and is trained by group-level cross-entropy against the future-compatibility target.

At inference, the assisting LLM supplies only next-token candidates; the selected reranker chooses one token from the joint pool, appends only that token, and immediately returns decoding to the SLM without generating or appending a future suffix.
The primary receiving model is Qwen3-1.7B, scale generalization is evaluated with Qwen3-0.6B, and Qwen3-32B is the assisting LLM; all base-model parameters remain frozen.

population.label: Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-0.6B receiving SLMs assisted by Qwen3-32B; all base parameters frozen

atoms.canonical_statement: End-to-end evaluation uses GSM8K, MATH-500, OlympiadBench, AIME 2024, and AIME 2025 with single-trajectory pass@1 accuracy as the primary metric and an unweighted Math Avg. across the five benchmarks.
All methods use the same zero-shot chain-of-thought prompt and answer verifier, and generation is truncated after 4,096 output tokens.

FutureBridge supervision is constructed from MATH training data and MATH validation is used to select the request threshold, reranker checkpoint, and future horizon before all choices are fixed for held-out benchmarks.
With Qwen3-1.7B as the receiving SLM, FutureBridge achieved 96.8% single-trajectory accuracy on GSM8K.

population.label: Five mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-1.7B receiving SLM and Qwen3-32B assisting LLM

atoms.canonical_statement: With Qwen3-1.7B as the receiving SLM, FutureBridge achieved 81.6% single-trajectory accuracy on MATH-500.

atoms.canonical_statement: With Qwen3-1.7B as the receiving SLM, FutureBridge achieved 43.5% single-trajectory accuracy on OlympiadBench.

atoms.canonical_statement: Under the matched token-only collaboration budget with Qwen3-1.7B, FutureBridge averaged 4.8 LLM calls per problem and 3.30x greedy-SLM latency; S2T also averaged 4.8 calls with 3.18x latency.

population.label: Token-only inference with Qwen3-1.7B receiving SLM

atoms.canonical_statement: FutureBridge's 3.30x latency was reported as 3.8% higher than S2T because of joint-pool scoring while improving Math Avg. by 1.24 points under the same average 4.8 LLM calls.

population.label: Token-only inference with Qwen3-1.7B receiving SLM

atoms.canonical_statement: Pairwise agreement with complete token-only candidate rollouts was 68.3% for FutureBridge, 69.7% for Direct-B_H, 61.2% for the LLM local score, and 56.9% for the SLM local score.

atoms.canonical_statement: With Qwen3-1.7B, restricting FutureBridge to an SLM-only candidate pool reduced Math Avg. from 50.38% to 47.9%, while an LLM-only pool reduced it to 48.3%.

population.label: Qwen3-1.7B evaluation on the reported ablation benchmark aggregate

atoms.canonical_statement: Using the same states, budget, and joint candidate pool, direct LLM local scoring achieved 47.2% Math Avg., versus 50.38% for FutureBridge.

population.label: Qwen3-1.7B matched candidate-selection ablation

atoms.canonical_statement: The distilled LLM-preference ablation achieved 46.7% Math Avg., compared with 50.38% for FutureBridge under matched architecture and optimization budget.

population.label: Qwen3-1.7B matched supervision-target ablation

atoms.canonical_statement: Increasing the shared-future training horizon from 16 to 64 tokens increased Math Avg. from 47.7% to 50.38%; increasing to 128 tokens yielded 50.5%.

atoms.canonical_statement: MATH validation selected H=64 for the deployed FutureBridge reranker even though H=128 produced a slightly higher reported aggregate score; deployment generates no future tokens.

atoms.canonical_statement: The external request policy uses entropy over the SLM distribution normalized on its top-64 support, with a threshold set to the 0.99 quantile on problem-disjoint MATH validation data and at most eight admitted intervention events per trajectory.
The 7,500 MATH training problems were split into 6,750 training problems and 750 validation problems before state collection to prevent prefixes from the same problem entering both subsets.

After answer verification, minimum 128-token future filtering, and candidate-group validation, 18,432 Qwen3-1.7B groups and 20,160 Qwen3-0.6B groups remained; overall retained fractions were 58.2% and 58.3%, respectively.

population.label: Logged admitted MATH states used for FutureBridge supervision construction

atoms.canonical_statement: The LoRA reranker uses rank 16, scaling 32, dropout 0.05 on query/key/value/output attention projections, a scalar head on the appended candidate token, AdamW at 2e-4, three epochs, target temperature 0.5, and three training seeds.
The main-table Math Avg. is reported as the mean across three training seeds without per-cell standard deviations.

One-time offline construction and training for the primary Qwen3-1.7B receiver totaled 51.0 H200 GPU-hours: 5.8 for state logging, 29.4 for verified-future generation, 8.6 for SLM compatibility scoring, and 7.2 for reranker optimization.

population.label: Offline FutureBridge supervision and reranker training for Qwen3-1.7B receiver

atoms.canonical_statement: At deployment with Qwen3-1.7B, FutureBridge considered an average joint pool of 13.2 candidates per intervention and used 78.1 GB GPU memory, versus an 8.0-token pool and 72.7 GB for S2T.

population.label: Per-problem token-only deployment with Qwen3-1.7B receiver

atoms.canonical_statement: At matched held-out GSM8K intervention states, the joint SLM-LLM top-8 pool contained a token yielding a correct complete SLM rollout in 88.2% of states, versus 79.4% for the LLM top-8 pool and 72.8% for the SLM top-8 pool.

population.label: Matched held-out GSM8K intervention states

atoms.canonical_statement: At matched held-out MATH-500 intervention states, the joint SLM-LLM top-8 pool contained a token yielding a correct complete SLM rollout in 63.4% of states, versus 54.1% for the LLM top-8 pool and 49.6% for the SLM top-8 pool.

population.label: Matched held-out MATH-500 intervention states

atoms.canonical_statement: At matched held-out OlympiadBench intervention states, the joint SLM-LLM top-8 pool contained a token yielding a correct complete SLM rollout in 59.5% of states, versus 50.7% for the LLM top-8 pool and 45.2% for the SLM top-8 pool.

population.label: Matched held-out OlympiadBench intervention states

atoms.canonical_statement: A size-matched SLM top-16 pool achieved a 48.0% Math Avg., 2.4 points below the joint SLM-LLM pool.

population.label: Qwen3-1.7B size-matched candidate-pool control

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that token-level collaboration should select interventions according to whether the receiving SLM can use them to continue reasoning, rather than according to the LLM's local preference alone.

The reported experiments support separating candidate coverage from candidate selection: the LLM can expand the available action space while an SLM-conditioned reranker chooses among the joint candidates.

extraction_limitations: No explicit funding disclosure, conflict-of-interest statement, or data/code availability statement was present in the inspected 10-page preprint content, so no atoms were created for those kinds.

The LiteratureAtom schema is oriented toward primary literature; for AI/ML quantitative results, population descriptors identify the evaluated model/benchmark setting and do not imply human participants.
The paper reports main-table Math Avg. as a three-seed mean without per-cell standard deviations; no uncertainty intervals were available for the principal benchmark cells.
FutureBridge evidence in this source is limited to mathematical reasoning benchmarks and Qwen3 model pairs; no non-mathematical deployment evaluation is reported in the source.
